title_prefix: Extraneous mkey records are not removed
mechanism: Core's WalletBatch::LoadWallet ends with a cleanup branch (refs/bitcoin/src/wallet/walletdb.cpp:1191-1203): when the wallet has WALLET_FLAG_DISABLE_PRIVATE_KEYS and HasEncryptionKeys() but !HaveCryptedKeys(), it logs "Detected extraneous encryption keys in this wallet without private keys", calls EraseMasterKey for every id in mapMasterKeys, returns DBErrors::CORRUPT if an erase fails, and clears mapMasterKeys. Our %load-wallet-records loads mkey rows into wallet-master-keys unconditionally (src/wallet/wallet.lisp:1088-1101) and load-wallet's post-load pass (:1266-1274) only pushes a warning when a disable-private-keys wallet still holds private keys; there is no branch anywhere under src/wallet/ that erases an mkey row (grepped: the only writers of wdb-key-mkey are encrypt-wallet and walletpassphrasechange). wallet-has-encryption-keys-p is defined as (plusp (hash-table-count (wallet-master-keys wallet))) (:240-243), so a surviving row makes the wallet report itself encrypted forever.
consequence: Such a wallet loads as encrypted and LOCKED although it holds no crypted keys, and there is no passphrase that can unlock it. getwalletinfo reports unlocked_until, and every RPC gated by wallet-ensure-unlocked fails with -13 -- including importdescriptors and rescanblockchain, both of which are entirely legitimate on a watch-only wallet and are the two operations such a wallet exists to perform. Exposure is nevertheless narrow: our createwallet RPC carries Core's guard (src/wallet/wallet.lisp:1600-1603 refuses a passphrase when private keys are disabled, matching refs/bitcoin/src/wallet/wallet.cpp:408-413) and encryptwallet refuses a disable-private-keys wallet with -16, so no path in this tree produces the file. It can only arrive hand-edited or through restorewallet from a dump made elsewhere. Worth noting for the fix: Core places the guard in CreateWallet, the function; ours is in the RPC handler only, and create-wallet the function will happily take :disable-private-keys t together with :passphrase, so the population stops being empty the moment a second caller appears.
evidence: Container /Users/sen/common-lisp/bl-ga11v-misc-s3d, warm image, probe-b.lisp. A disable-private-keys wallet was created, one extraneous mkey row planted with wdb-key-mkey/wdb-mkey-value, then unloaded and reloaded. Output: (:FRESH-DISABLE-PRIVATE-KEYS :HAS-ENCRYPTION-KEYS NIL :LOCKED NIL) (:ENCRYPTWALLET-REFUSES (-16 "Error: wallet does not contain private keys, nothing to encrypt.")) (:MKEYS-ON-DISK-BEFORE-LOAD (1)) (:AFTER-RELOAD :HAS-ENCRYPTION-KEYS T :LOCKED T :MASTER-KEY-COUNT 1 :DISABLE-PRIVATE-KEYS T :HAVE-CRYPTED-KEYS NIL) (:GETWALLETINFO-UNLOCKED-UNTIL 0) (:IMPORTDESCRIPTORS-ON-RELOADED-WATCHONLY (-13 "Error: Please enter the wallet passphrase with walletpassphrase first.")) (:RESCANBLOCKCHAIN-ON-RELOADED-WATCHONLY (-13 ...)) (:MKEYS-STILL-ON-DISK-AFTER-LOAD (1)). The reload reproduces exactly Core's trigger condition -- disable-private-keys set, has-encryption-keys true, no crypted keys -- and the rows survive the load. Ours: src/wallet/wallet.lisp:1088-1101, :1245-1274, :240-243. Core: refs/bitcoin/src/wallet/walletdb.cpp:1191-1203.
fix_shape: Add Core's branch at the end of load-wallet's post-load pass, after the existing private-keys warning and only when the record load reported no corruption (Core skips every cleanup when result != LOAD_OK): if the wallet has +wallet-flag-disable-private-keys+ and wallet-has-encryption-keys-p is true and no SPKM holds any crypted key, log Core's line verbatim, delete every mkey row under a single LevelDB write batch keyed by the ids in wallet-master-keys, and clrhash wallet-master-keys. A failed delete must fail the load the way Core returns CORRUPT, not be swallowed, because a half-erased set leaves the same wrong state. Move the createwallet passphrase guard down into create-wallet where Core keeps it, so the invariant belongs to the function rather than to one caller. A regression test plants an mkey row in a disable-private-keys wallet, reloads, and asserts wallet-has-encryption-keys-p is NIL, the row is gone from the database, and importdescriptors succeeds.
